maria: Heads-up — we started seeing a p99 latency spike on prod around 12:02 UTC after the adaptive windowing heuristic rollout. p50 ~ 70ms (unchanged), p95 up from ~85ms -> 220ms, p99 jumped ~250ms -> ~860ms. Throughput on the affected pool down ~18%. Not sure if this is batch formation delay or KV churn. see dashboard: https://go/realtime-p99
kevin: seeing same. KV cache hit rate on pool-redwood-03 dropped ~2.8% around the same time. Also noticed average batch sizes increased a bit but variance went up — more very large batches and some tiny ones. Hypothesis: adaptive-window is waiting longer to accumulate tokens then forming huge batches that stall kernel selection.
zheng: quick look at runtime logs shows a few kernel picks falling back to fallback_sgemm for seq_len 1024 path, which is slower on A100 with our optimized matmul. snippet:
```
[12:03:15] kernel-selector: seq_len=1024 -> selected=fallback_sgemm (score: 0.42)
[12:03:15] kernel-selector: seq_len=512 -> selected=fast_qk (score: 0.88)
```
That fallback correlates with the big batches. Could be an integer overflow in batch token accounting causing wrong kernel bucket.
olivia: I ran a quick perf collect on a canary replica at ~12:10. flamegraph shows long tail in `kv_cache::lookup_or_fetch` and also stalls in `batch_window::wait_for_budget`. Uploading trace: https://go/prof/1765122330 (perm: eng-runtime).
infra-bot: deploybot: rollout adaptive-windowing v2 -> prod started by @kevin at 2025-11-09T11:50:12Z. 80% of pool targeted.
sre-oncall: can we throttle the rollout? current error budget still fine but latency SLOs are breached. propose pause and roll back to v1 for the pool.
maria: value change that landed with v2: queue_budget_target went from "65536" to "24576" (tokens) to bias shorter waits. That was intended to reduce cost but maybe it interacts badly with adaptive window growth.
kevin: if queue_budget_target is too small, adaptive window will expand horizon to hit token goal, but with skewed arrival rates it might end up creating very uneven batches. Also RK (routing) could be combining requests across model variants, causing kernel selector to get weird mixed seq distributions.
zheng: can reproduce locally by toggling queue_budget_target=24576 + enable adaptive-window. Repro steps:
```
# start local runtime with canary config
./bin/runtime --config=configs/canary.json --override adaptive_window=true queue_budget_target=24576
# run replay trace (small load)
./tools/replay --trace traces/serve-peak-11-09.json --concurrency 48
```
Results: p99 ~780ms and kernel fallback log spikes.
olivia: I also checked KV metrics — prefix coalescing reduced hit locality because windowing grouped requests from different sessions more often; that increased cache misses. Hit rate drop matches zheng's local repro when mixing session ids.
maria: plan: 1) pause rollout to 50% on pool-redwood-03, 2) revert queue_budget_target to 49152 on that pool, 3) enable sticky-kernel-selection flag (so kernel chosen per batch shape is cached for X minutes), 4) run canary traffic replay for 30m and collect flamegraphs.
kevin: +1. I'll patch the canary script to also log `kernel-bucket` histograms and token-accounting checksums to catch overflow.
zheng: I'll run the revert + sticky-kernel canary now and attach profile. If that fixes p99 we know it's the token budgeting->kernel select path.
sre-oncall: schedule: revert at 12:40 UTC, canary run 12:45-13:15, report 13:25. If p99 back to baseline roll forward revert to production.
maria: thanks. If anyone sees other oddities (CPU steal, driver resets) ping here. :eyes:
kevin: noted. will post logs and the kernel-bucket output once run completes. :thumbsup:
